headline: A short-term spending bill that keeps federal agencies funded through December 28, 2020, so the government does not shut down when the prior stopgap expires.
what_it_does: The bill provides continuing funding for federal agencies for fiscal year 2021 through December 28, 2020. It is a continuing resolution, which is a temporary extension of funding used when full spending bills are not yet finished. Without it, funding would lapse when the existing stopgap expired on December 21, 2020, and agencies would have to shut down.

who_it_affects.how: They can keep operating and spending money at current levels through December 28, 2020, instead of closing when the prior funding ran out.
Those whose paychecks depend on agency appropriations are protected from a lapse in funding during this period.
Programs and services run by federal agencies can continue without interruption through the extension period.

when_it_takes_effect: Funding is extended through December 28, 2020, as the summary describes; the exact start date is not stated in the summary.
